html:
In 1206 a great assembly of Mongol chiefs, a kurultai, met near the source of the Onon River and proclaimed Temüjin ruler of all the peoples of the steppe, with the title Genghis Khan. The date is usually taken as the founding of the Mongol Empire.

It came after twenty years of war. Temüjin had beaten the Tatars, the Kereit of his old patron Toghrul, and the Naimans, and his rival Jamukha had been handed over and executed. For the first time the Mongols, Tatars, Kereit, Naimans, Merkits and others were under one ruler.

The meaning of the title is uncertain. Some read it as "firm" or "fierce" ruler, others link it to a word for the ocean, meaning "universal".

At and after the assembly, Genghis Khan set up the order that made the conquests possible:

  • The old tribes were broken up and people were put in army units of a thousand, each led by a trusted commander.
  • He created a large personal guard, which also served as a school for officers.
  • He named a chief judge and issued decrees later known as the Yassa.

The Secret History of the Mongols describes the assembly and lists the commanders rewarded there. Within a few years the new state attacked Western Xia and then the Jin dynasty of north China.
